question:
The sum of the total number of protons and neutrons present in the nucleus of an atom is known as -

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Avogadro number
Gauss number
Atomic number
Mass number
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Mass number

Explanation:
The sum of the total number of protons and neutrons present in the nucleus of an atom is known as the Mass Number (A). It represents the majority of an atom's mass since electrons contribute negligibly. For example, carbon-12 has 6 protons and 6 neutrons, giving it a mass number of 12. The mass number is crucial in defining isotopes of an element, which have the same atomic number but different mass numbers.

Extra Facts:
The Atomic Number (Z) denotes the number of protons in the nucleus, while the Avogadro Number (6.022 × 10²³) represents the number of particles (atoms, molecules, ions) in one mole of a substance. The Gauss Number is related to magnetic flux density and is irrelevant here.

[RRB NTPC CBT]

solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है द्रव्यमान संख्या

Explanation:
किसी परमाणु के नाभिक में मौजूद प्रोटॉन और न्यूट्रॉन की कुल संख्या को द्रव्यमान संख्या (Mass Number) कहा जाता है। यह परमाणु के द्रव्यमान का मुख्य स्रोत होता है क्योंकि इलेक्ट्रॉन का द्रव्यमान नगण्य होता है। द्रव्यमान संख्या को 'A' से प्रदर्शित किया जाता है। उदाहरण के लिए, कार्बन-12 में 6 प्रोटॉन और 6 न्यूट्रॉन होते हैं, इसलिए इसकी द्रव्यमान संख्या 12 होती है। यह परमाणु के आइसोटोप को परिभाषित करने में भी महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाता है।

question:
Which radioactive isotope has a half-life of 5770 years, which is commonly used to estimate the age of organic materials such as paper and parchment ?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: 9C
12C
14C
17C
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 14C

Explanation:
Carbon-14 (14C) is a radioactive isotope with a half-life of approximately 5770 years. It is used in radiocarbon dating to estimate the age of organic materials such as paper, parchment, wood, and bones. This technique works on the principle that living organisms absorb carbon-14 from the atmosphere, but after death, this absorption stops, and the carbon-14 begins to decay. By measuring the decay rate, the age of the sample is determined.

Extra Facts:
- Carbon-14 is formed in the atmosphere when nitrogen-14 interacts with cosmic rays.
- This technique is useful for dating samples up to 50,000 years old.
- Willard Libby developed the radiocarbon dating technique in 1949 and won the Nobel Prize in 1960 for it.
- Carbon-12 and Carbon-13 are stable isotopes, whereas Carbon-14 is radioactive.

☛ What is the half-life of Carbon-14? → 5770 years
☛ Who developed the radiocarbon dating technique? → Willard Libby
☛ Which carbon isotopes are stable? → Carbon-12 and Carbon-13
☛ What is the maximum limit of radiocarbon dating? → 50,000 years

question:
Which of these scientists discovered the radioactive element radium ?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Amedeo Avogadro
Marie Curie
Louis Pasteur
Leonard Euler
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Marie Curie

Explanation:
The radioactive element radium (Ra) was discovered in 1898 by Marie Curie and her husband Pierre Curie. It is a highly radioactive element found in uranium ore pitchblende. Marie Curie conducted groundbreaking research on radioactivity, earning her the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1903 and in Chemistry in 1911. The discovery of radioactivity revolutionized modern physics and medical science.

Extra Facts:
Radium (Ra) is an alkaline earth metal with atomic number 88. It is extremely rare in nature and is used in cancer treatment (radiotherapy). Marie Curie's discoveries significantly contributed to nuclear physics and radiotherapy. Her daughter, Irène Joliot-Curie, also researched radioactivity and won a Nobel Prize.

☛ Who was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize? → Marie Curie

☛ What are the three types of radioactive decay? → Alpha, Beta, Gamma

question:
Which radioactive isotope has a half-life of 5770 years, which is commonly used to estimate the age of organic materials such as paper and parchment ?

[SSC CHSL 2023]
options: C9
C12
C14
C17
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is C14

Explanation:
Carbon-14 (C14) is a radioactive isotope with a half-life of approximately 5770 years. It is used in radiocarbon dating to estimate the age of organic materials such as paper, parchment, wood, and bones. This technique is based on the principle that living organisms absorb carbon-14 from the atmosphere, and after death, this absorption stops. Over time, the amount of carbon-14 decreases, allowing scientists to calculate the age of the sample by measuring the remaining carbon-14.

Extra Facts:
Carbon-14 is formed in the atmosphere when cosmic rays interact with nitrogen-14. This dating method is effective for samples up to 50,000 years old. It was discovered by Willard Libby in 1949, earning him the Nobel Prize in 1960. Carbon-14 dating has been used to determine the age of Egyptian mummies, prehistoric fossils, and ancient artifacts. The technique revolutionized archaeology and geology by providing a reliable method for dating organic materials.

question:
Which of the following statements is NOT correct regarding Rutherford's nuclear model of an atom?

[SSC CHSL 2022]
options: The size of the nucleus is very large as compared to the size of the atom.
The electrons revolve around the nucleus in circular paths.
There is a positively charged center in an atom called the nucleus.
Nearly all the mass of an atom resides in the nucleus.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The size of the nucleus is very large as compared to the size of the atom.

Explanation:
According to Rutherford's nuclear model of the atom, most of the mass of the atom is concentrated in the nucleus, which is positively charged. Electrons revolve around the nucleus in circular paths. However, the size of the nucleus is very small compared to the size of the atom. If the atom is imagined to be the size of a football stadium, the nucleus would be about the size of a pea. Therefore, the statement 'The size of the nucleus is very large as compared to the size of the atom' is incorrect.

Extra Facts:
Rutherford proposed his atomic model in 1911. Through his gold foil experiment, he proved that most of the atom is empty space and its positive charge is concentrated in the nucleus. This model rejected Thomson's 'plum pudding model'. However, Rutherford's model could not explain the stability of electrons, which was later resolved by Bohr's model.

☛ What is the total charge of an atom? → Neutral (zero)

question:
There are three isotopes of hydrogen atoms, namely Protium, Deuterium and Tritium. The respective atomic number and mass number of the isotope Tritium is:

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: 1, 1
3, 1
1, 2
1, 3
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1, 3

Explanation:
Hydrogen has three isotopes:
1. Protium - Atomic number (Z) = 1, Mass number (A) = 1
2. Deuterium - Atomic number (Z) = 1, Mass number (A) = 2
3. Tritium - Atomic number (Z) = 1, Mass number (A) = 3

Tritium contains 1 proton and 2 neutrons, giving it a mass number of 3. The atomic number remains the same (1) for all hydrogen isotopes as it represents the number of protons in the nucleus.

Extra Facts:
- Isotopes are atoms of the same element with the same atomic number but different mass numbers.
- Tritium is a radioactive isotope with a half-life of about 12.3 years.
- Deuterium is used in making heavy water (D2O), which acts as a moderator in nuclear reactors.

question:
The number of ______ is equal to the difference between the mass number of the atom and the atomic number.

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Protons
Electrons
Neutrons
Both protons and electrons
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Neutrons

Explanation:
The mass number (A) of an atom is the sum of protons (p) and neutrons (n), while the atomic number (Z) represents only the number of protons. Therefore, to find the number of neutrons, the atomic number is subtracted from the mass number.
Formula:
n = A – Z
where,
n = number of neutrons,
A = mass number,
Z = atomic number.
For example, carbon (C) has an atomic number of 6 and a mass number of 12, so the number of neutrons = 12 – 6 = 6.

Extra Facts:
1. Neutrons are electrically neutral particles, while protons are positively charged and electrons are negatively charged.
2. Isotopes are elements with the same atomic number but different mass numbers due to varying neutron counts.
3. The most common isotope of hydrogen, protium (¹H), has no neutrons.

Explanation:

Extra Facts:

question:
Protium, deuterium and tritium are the naturally occurring isotopes of:

[SSC CGL 2019]
options: carbon
hydrogen
nitrogen
gold
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is hydrogen

Explanation:
Protium (¹H), deuterium (²H or D), and tritium (³H or T) are the three naturally occurring isotopes of hydrogen.
- Protium is the most common isotope of hydrogen, with a nucleus containing only one proton and no neutrons.
- Deuterium has one proton and one neutron and is also called 'heavy hydrogen.' It is used as a moderator in nuclear reactors.
- Tritium is radioactive and contains one proton and two neutrons. It is used in biological tracers and nuclear fusion.

Extra Facts:
- Hydrogen is the most abundant element in the universe and the first element in the periodic table.
- Deuterium oxide (D₂O), known as 'heavy water,' is used as a neutron moderator in nuclear reactors.
- Tritium has a half-life of about 12.3 years and decays into helium-3 via beta decay.

Strontium-89 (Sr-89) is used for the treatment of metastatic bone cancer. It is a radioactive isotope that emits beta particles. Its half-life is approximately 50.5 days, making it suitable for treatment. This therapy is part of palliative care and provides pain relief.

question:
Neutrons are present in the nucleus of all atoms, except -

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Carbon
Oxygen
Nitrogen
Hydrogen
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Hydrogen

Explanation:
The neutron is a subatomic particle found in the nucleus of an atom along with protons. The most common isotope of hydrogen, protium (¹H), consists of only one proton and no neutrons. Therefore, hydrogen is the only element whose nucleus does not contain neutrons. All other elements (such as carbon, oxygen, nitrogen) have both protons and neutrons in their nucleus. The mass of a neutron is approximately equal to that of a proton, but it is electrically neutral.

Extra Facts:
1. Other isotopes of hydrogen, such as deuterium (²H) and tritium (³H), contain 1 and 2 neutrons respectively, but these are found in very small quantities in nature.
2. The neutron was discovered by James Chadwick in 1932.
3. Neutrons play a crucial role in sustaining the chain reaction of nuclear fission in atomic reactors.

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Plutonium

Explanation:
Plutonium (Pu) is a radioactive actinide element discovered by Glenn T. Seaborg and his team in 1940. It is used as a heat source for sensitive electrical components in satellites and as a power source for satellites. Plutonium-238 (Pu-238) is specifically used in Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generators (RTGs), which provide long-term energy to spacecraft and satellites. Pu-238 has a half-life of 87.7 years, making it ideal for prolonged energy production. It emits alpha particles, which pose minimal radiation hazards, making it safe for space applications.

Extra Facts:
Plutonium is not only used in space applications but also in nuclear weapons and reactors. Pu-239 is a fissile isotope used in nuclear fission reactions. Plutonium was named after the planet Pluto, as it follows uranium (named after Uranus) in the periodic table. It is a shiny, silvery metal that oxidizes when exposed to air.

question:
What is the characteristic of isotopes?

[SSC MTS 2022]
options: Same neutron and same proton
Same atomic number and different mass number
Same atomic number and same mass number
Same neutron and different proton
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Same atomic number and different mass number

Explanation:
Isotopes are atoms of the same element that have the same atomic number (number of protons) but a different mass number (protons + neutrons). This difference arises due to a variation in the number of neutrons. For example, carbon isotopes C-12 and C-14 both have 6 protons, but C-12 has 6 neutrons while C-14 has 8 neutrons, giving them mass numbers of 12 and 14, respectively. Isotopes exhibit similar chemical properties because chemical behavior primarily depends on the electronic configuration, which is determined by the number of protons.

Extra Facts:
Isotopes have diverse applications, such as radioactive isotopes (C-14, U-235) being used in carbon dating and nuclear energy. Hydrogen isotopes (Protium, Deuterium, Tritium) include Protium (no neutrons), Deuterium (1 neutron), and Tritium (2 neutrons). Isotopes are also used in medicine (radiotherapy), industry (tracer studies), and scientific research.

समस्थानिक एक ही तत्व के वे परमाणु होते हैं जिनकी परमाणु संख्या (प्रोटॉन की संख्या) समान होती है, लेकिन द्रव्यमान संख्या (प्रोटॉन + न्यूट्रॉन की संख्या) भिन्न होती है। यह अंतर न्यूट्रॉन की संख्या में भिन्नता के कारण होता है। उदाहरण के लिए, कार्बन के समस्थानिक C-12 और C-14 में दोनों में 6 प्रोटॉन होते हैं, लेकिन C-12 में 6 न्यूट्रॉन और C-14 में 8 न्यूट्रॉन होते हैं। इस प्रकार, इनकी द्रव्यमान संख्या क्रमशः 12 और 14 होती है। समस्थानिकों के रासायनिक गुण समान होते हैं क्योंकि रासायनिक गुण मुख्य रूप से इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास पर निर्भर करते हैं, जो प्रोटॉन की संख्या से निर्धारित होता है।

प्रोटियम हाइड्रोजन का सबसे सामान्य और हल्का आइसोटोप है। इसका परमाणु क्रमांक 1 है, जिसका अर्थ है कि इसमें 1 प्रोटॉन और 1 इलेक्ट्रॉन होता है। प्रोटियम में कोई न्यूट्रॉन नहीं होता है, इसलिए इसका द्रव्यमान संख्या भी 1 होता है। यह हाइड्रोजन के तीन आइसोटोप्स (प्रोटियम, ड्यूटीरियम और ट्रिटियम) में से एक है। ड्यूटीरियम में 1 न्यूट्रॉन और ट्रिटियम में 2 न्यूट्रॉन होते हैं।

Extra Facts:
हाइड्रोजन ब्रह्मांड में सबसे प्रचुर मात्रा में पाया जाने वाला तत्व है। प्रोटियम हाइड्रोजन का 99.98% हिस्सा बनाता है। यह सितारों में नाभिकीय संलयन का प्राथमिक ईंधन है। हाइड्रोजन का उपयोग ईंधन सेल, अमोनिया उत्पादन और पेट्रोलियम शोधन में किया जाता है। प्रोटियम का नाभिक केवल एक प्रोटॉन से बना होता है, जो इसे सबसे सरल परमाणु नाभिक बनाता है।

question:
An isotope of which of the following is used in the treatment of cancer?

[SSC CHSL 2022]
options: Cobalt
Aluminum
Nickel
Iron
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Cobalt

Explanation:
Cobalt-60 (Co-60) is a radioactive isotope used in the treatment of cancer. It emits gamma rays, which are used in radiotherapy to destroy cancer cells. Cobalt-60 is used in teletherapy machines, which can target deep-seated tumors in the body. This isotope is produced by neutron bombardment of cobalt-59. Its half-life is 5.27 years, making it suitable for medical use.

Extra Facts:
Other isotopes used in radiotherapy include iodine-131 (thyroid cancer) and cesium-137. Cobalt-60 is also used in industrial applications such as food preservation and sterilization of medical equipment. It plays a significant role in nuclear fission reactions. The gamma rays emitted by cobalt-60 are high-energy and can penetrate deep into tissues.

question_hi:
निम्नलिखित में से किसके समस्थानिक ( isotope ) का उपयोग कैंसर के उपचार में किया जाता है?

[SSC CHSL 2022]
options_hi: कोबाल्ट
एल्यूमीनियम
निकेल
लोहा
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है कोबाल्ट

Explanation:
कोबाल्ट-60 (Co-60) एक रेडियोधर्मी समस्थानिक है जिसका उपयोग कैंसर के उपचार में किया जाता है। यह गामा किरणें उत्सर्जित करता है, जो कैंसर कोशिकाओं को नष्ट करने के लिए रेडियोथेरेपी में प्रयोग किया जाता है। कोबाल्ट-60 का उपयोग टेलीथेरेपी मशीनों में किया जाता है, जो शरीर के अंदर गहरे स्थित ट्यूमर को लक्षित करने में सक्षम होती हैं। यह समस्थानिक कोबाल्ट-59 के न्यूट्रॉन बमबारी से उत्पन्न होता है। इसकी अर्धायु 5.27 वर्ष होती है, जो इसे चिकित्सा उपयोग के लिए उपयुक्त बनाती है।

Extra Facts:
रेडियोथेरेपी में उपयोग किए जाने वाले अन्य समस्थानिकों में आयोडीन-131 (थायरॉयड कैंसर) और सीज़ियम-137 शामिल हैं। कोबाल्ट-60 का उपयोग औद्योगिक अनुप्रयोगों जैसे खाद्य संरक्षण और मेडिकल उपकरणों की स्टरलाइज़ेशन में भी किया जाता है। यह परमाणु विखंडन प्रतिक्रियाओं में भी महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाता है। कोबाल्ट-60 की गामा किरणें उच्च ऊर्जा वाली होती हैं, जो ऊतकों में गहराई तक प्रवेश कर सकती हैं।
